sections.h2: How did Broward County come to exist?
sections.html:
Broward was carved out of Dade and Palm Beach territory and became Florida's 51st county on October 1, 1915. According to a city of Pompano Beach history, it measured 24 miles north to south and 48 miles east to west, held about 4,700 people packed within a mile or two of the coast, and had only three incorporated towns: Dania, Pompano and Fort Lauderdale.

Opening day brought a parade, a concert and picnic lunches in Fort Lauderdale, the new seat, along with speeches by the first commissioners.

Residents had wanted to call it Everglades County. Instead it took the name of a governor who championed draining the Everglades, which the history calls ironic. Northern Dade residents had complained that their tax dollars favored Miami, and a local vote on alcohol sales also pushed Miami-area voters toward a new county.

sections.h2: What was here before the county?
sections.html:
The land passed through several counties. Under the first territorial government it belonged to a huge St. Johns County, later to Mosquito County, and then to a southeast coast county first meant to be Pinckney County and renamed Dade after the 1835 ambush that started the Second Seminole War. Palm Beach became the 47th county in 1909 and briefly reached south to Pompano.

The Florida East Coast Railway reached Palm Beach in 1894 and Miami in 1896, ending the area's isolation and bringing farm towns along the tracks. Before that, the first major road linking Miami and Lantana, a nine-foot gravel track, was built in 1892.

sections.h2: How big and varied is Broward today?
sections.html:
The county now includes 31 municipalities. Fort Lauderdale serves as seat and biggest city, covering more than 33 square miles with 183,146 residents, according to the city. It was incorporated on March 27, 1911, and sits framed by seven miles of beach and the Everglades, with the Intracoastal Waterway, the New River and a canal system running through the middle.

The city names Las Olas Boulevard and the Riverwalk arts district, with the Broward Center for the Performing Arts, the Museum of Discovery and Science, the NSU Art Museum and History Fort Lauderdale, and notes downtown campuses of Broward College, Florida Atlantic University and Florida International University.

For a seller, the variety shows up in values. A canal-front home near Las Olas and a condo in a western city share a county appraiser and tax collector but not a market.

The property appraiser sets assessed values and approves exemptions. It states plainly that it does not mail tax bills and does not set or collect taxes. Billing and collection belong to the Broward County Tax Collector, reachable at (954) 357-4829 or revenue@browardtax.org, as printed on the appraiser's home page.

Deed recording runs through the county's official records, and the appraiser's FAQ page has a deed topic for questions on adding or removing an owner or getting copies of recorded documents. Counter service is on weekdays.

sections.h2: When can Broward owners file for 2027 homestead?
sections.html:
The appraiser prints a timely filing period of March 3, 2026 through March 1, 2027 for the 2027 exemption. It applies to owners who held title and made the house their permanent home after January 1, 2026.

Someone who misses March 1 has until September 20, 2027, and the office notes that s. 196.011(8) allows no later date, even with good cause. Because the dates belong to one tax year, use the appraiser's page as the reference for later years.

sections.h2: What free tools does the Broward appraiser offer to sellers and buyers?
sections.html:
The site carries several that a house sale can use.

  • A Home Buyer's Tax Estimator that approximates the bill after a reassessment, which helps a seller explain why a buyer's taxes will differ.
  • A Portability Estimator for owners moving a homestead benefit to a new Florida home.
  • Owner Alert, a free message when a filing that changes who owns your parcel reaches the appraiser, built to flag scams.
  • A catastrophic structural damage report form for a home left uninhabitable for at least 30 days by a catastrophic event.
  • Tabs for Senior Citizens, Appeals and Petitions, Market Sales and Important Dates, and a posted Property Owner Bill of Rights.

Its crucial buyer notice tells purchasers not to expect the seller's taxes to carry over, since the new owner starts at full market value.

sections.h2: How does moving or selling affect a Broward homestead?
sections.html:
The sale ends the homestead cap on the old house. Someone buying another Florida home can file Form DR-501T alongside the new application, provided the new homestead starts inside the three-year window. A 2026 act amends the portability section for the 2027 roll, so ask the appraiser's portability staff what applies to your move.

Rentals face a yearly ceiling of 10 percent, so a landlord's gap between assessed and market value is usually narrower than a long-time homesteader's.

sections.h2: Which relief programs can a Broward owner ask about?
sections.html: Age and veteran relief varies by ordinance and service record, so the Senior Citizens tab on the appraiser's site is the quickest place to learn what a particular address can claim. The state also offers a $5,000 reduction for disabled former servicemembers, and a deferral through the collector with a March 31 filing date.

sections.h2: What if a Broward bill goes unpaid?
sections.html: Delinquency starts April 1, and the collector auctions certificates for the lowest bid rate by June 1. If a tax deed notice shows up, call the collector at once. A seller who clears the balance before any deed application avoids the auction altogether, and the title agent can pay it from proceeds. Homestead rules on small balances and opening bids sit in s. 197.502.

sections.h2: Where does a Broward value challenge go?
sections.html: The appraiser's Appeals and Petitions section explains the route. A formal petition goes to the clerk. Property owners get 25 days from the August notice, and an exemption denial carries its own 30 day clock from the letter.

sections.h2: What should heirs or owners with unwanted occupants know?
sections.html:
An heir can call the appraiser at (954) 357-5579 to learn how a transfer on death is treated, since some transfers are exceptions to the reset.

Uninvited occupants are a separate matter. The sheriff handles a verified complaint under s. 82.036, which carries conditions such as no tenancy and no pending litigation, and adverse possession (s. 95.18) needs seven years.

faqs.a: The Broward County Tax Collector. The appraiser says it neither sends bills nor collects taxes.

faqs.q: What is the late-filing limit for a 2027 Broward homestead?
faqs.a: September 20, 2027, with no later date allowed under s. 196.011(8).

faqs.q: Can I file my Broward homestead online?
faqs.a: Yes, through the appraiser's online homestead page. Email, fax, mail and phone help are also listed.
It is a free service that notifies you when a document changing your property's ownership is received by the appraiser.

faqs.q: When does a Broward bill turn delinquent?
faqs.a: April 1, per the state calendar, with certificates sold by June 1.
